newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Salmon sets option to sell Aquacultivos.
newsitem.headline: NZ Salmon sets option to sell Aquacultivos.

text.p: New Zealand Salmon said on Friday it had agreed a sales option for its Chilean salmon farming operations held through its 50 percent interest in Aquacultivos, based in Puerto Montt, Chile.
Aquacultivos has agreed an option with Mainstream Salomones y Alimentos (Mainstream) for the purchase of all of the shares of Aquacultivos.
Mainstream is a significant player in the Chilean Salmon industry and is listed on the Chilean Stock Exchange, NZS said.
The option extends until August 1 and would allow it to buy all of the Aquacultivos shares based on a price equal to the book value of the assets of the company as at June 30.
The purchase would be via an issue of Mainstream shares.
NZS said the current trade price of NZ Salmon shares was likely to be reflected in the net proceeds attributed to its interest in Aquacultivos. It has no other trading assets.

"Given the liquidity problems (in Aquacultivos) that have arisen out of a depressed market situation, and a thorough assessment of the alternatives facing Aquacultivos, the Mainstream option is considered to be the best route to take,"

"Combining Aquacultivos assets with those of Mainstream is in accord with earlier sentiments expressed by directors relating to the compelling need for rationalisation in the Chilean salmon industry," NZS said.
It said in the six months to June 30, Aquacultivos had experienced "significant difficulties".
"Since that announcement, market conditions have continued to weaken and as reported... directors see little prospect of conditions improving in the near future."
